subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nanoscale Drug Resistance
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nanoscale Drug Resistance.

hook.text: Cancer cells pump out drugs with efflux proteins — nanoparticles sneak past these pumps by entering differently.

buildup.text: Free drugs enter through membrane transporters — the same pumps that eject them. Nanoparticles use endocytosis.

discovery.text: Once inside via endocytosis, the drug releases deep in the cell — bypassing efflux pumps entirely.

twist.text: Cells can still develop resistance — some alter endocytosis itself or degrade drugs in lysosomes.

climax.text: Combination nanoparticles deliver a drug plus a pump inhibitor together — attacking resistance on two fronts.

punchline.text: When cancer pumps out the drug, nanoparticles take a different door.

quiz.question: How do nanoparticles help overcome cancer drug resistance?
options: They use higher doses of the same drug
They enter cells via endocytosis, bypassing efflux pumps that eject free drugs
They permanently disable the cancer cell's DNA
